title: The Trench
hook: Ten thousand soldiers marched on Madinah. The Muslims dug a ditch, hungry, with their Prophet ﷺ digging beside them.

screens.text: **About ten thousand soldiers were marching on Madinah.** The Muslims didn't build a wall. They dug a ditch, hungry, and the Prophet ﷺ dug right beside them.

**A city surrounded.** About five years after the hijra, Quraysh and allied tribes, about ten thousand strong, came against Madinah. The Muslims, about three thousand, dug a trench across the city's open side [IslamQA 201120; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The siege lasted about a month [Yaqeen (Hate)].

options.feedback: Right. The newcomer from Persia had the idea, and the Prophet ﷺ took it [Yaqeen (Salman)].
Not quite. Quraysh were the attackers. The idea is credited to Salman, a Persian convert.

options.text: Nobody; it was always the plan
options.feedback: Not quite. The early biographers credit Salman al-Farisi, a convert from Persia.

screens.text: **Digging beside them.** He carried earth until dust covered his skin, reciting prayers for steadfastness [Bukhari 2837]. When they hit a rock no one could break, he came down, a stone tied to his stomach from three days of hunger, and broke it [Bukhari 4101].
A siege, a ditch, and a wind.

events.title: The siege
events.text: Fear grips the city: hearts reached the throats [Q 33:10].

events.title: A wind
events.text: Allah sends a wind and forces they could not see [Q 33:9].

events.title: They leave
events.text: The coalition gives up and goes home [IslamQA 11575].

screens.text: **The Qur'an remembers the fear.** It describes that time honestly: *"when eyes shifted [in fear], and hearts reached the throats"*. Then Allah sent *"a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see"* [Q 33:10; Q 33:9, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: In the end, the armies gave up and went home [IslamQA 11575].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- A coalition of Quraysh and allied tribes (about 10,000) came against Madinah; the Muslims (about 3,000) dug a trench across its open side [IslamQA 201120; IslamQA 11575]; the siege lasted about a month [Yaqeen (How Muhammad Confronted Hate)]. Year: most say 5 AH, Musa ibn 'Uqbah says 4 AH, so say "about five years after the hijra". (scholar question Q39)
- The early biographers credit Salman al-Farisi, a Persian convert, with the idea [Yaqeen (Salman al-Farsi)].
- He carried earth until dust covered him, reciting lines asking Allah for tranquility and steadfastness [Bukhari 2837]; with a stone tied to his stomach after three days without food, he broke a rock they couldn't [Bukhari 4101].
- The Qur'an describes the fear and how Allah sent a wind and unseen forces [Q 33:9–11]; the believers said "This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us" [Q 33:22]. The coalition left [IslamQA 11575].
- His rules of war applied: no killing of women or children [Bukhari 3015].
- On the march to Banu Qurayzah afterwards, the Companions understood his instruction about 'Asr two ways, and he blamed neither group [Bukhari 4119]; Day 40 uses this.

**Banu Qurayzah (AI guide only beyond the one screen line)** (scholar question Q38)
- Banu Qurayzah, a Jewish tribe of Madinah bound by treaty, broke it during the siege and sided with the attackers [IslamQA 201120]. Afterwards they were besieged (about 25 days per SeekersGuidance) and agreed to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, a former ally whom they chose [SeekersGuidance (Banu Qurayza)].
- Sa'd ruled that their fighting men be executed and the women and children taken captive [Bukhari 4122]. SeekersGuidance notes this matched the treaty-breaking rule in the tribe's own scripture (Deuteronomy 20:12–14), that boys who hadn't reached puberty were spared, and that some were granted amnesty [SeekersGuidance (Banu Qurayza)]. Q 33:26 refers to it.
- Tell it calmly, as treason in wartime judged by an arbiter they chose. **Give no number** (the sirah's figures vary and our sources don't confirm one). No "they deserved it" framing. Never connect it to Jews today (Day 73 rule). Offer the imam for anything further.

**Likely questions**
- *"What happened with Banu Qurayzah?"* Use the calm summary above in 3–4 lines, then offer the imam. (scholar question Q38)
- *"Wasn't this violent?"* Day 71 frame: the city was under siege by an army; the Muslims dug and defended. (scholar question Q39)
- *"Who was Salman?"* A Persian convert who became Muslim in Madinah [Yaqeen (Salman al-Farsi)]; the early biographers credit him with the trench.
- *"I'm new. Do my ideas count?"* Yes; offer them humbly to the right people.

**Escalate:** Banu Qurayzah beyond the summary (Q38); any question about fighting today (fixed policy).

**Don't**
- Don't give a number for Banu Qurayzah, use graphic detail, or say "they deserved it".
- Don't connect any of this to Jewish people today.
- Don't put Q 33:26 or Bukhari 4122 on a screen.
